title: 4D-STEM and Ptychography from Room Temperature to 8.8 Kelvin
content: 4D-STEM including ptychography has emerged as a powerful imaging modality [1-3], and a promising direction is the application of these techniques to study low-temperature phenomena. Previous efforts to study quantum phenomena and correlated systems below liquid nitrogen temperatures [4] have typically been compromised by instrumental instability, motivating a new approach.
